examples.en: That child was called a piano prodigy.
It was in the news that a prodigy had appeared.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 수학 신동이라는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, I have been called a math prodigy.

examples.ko: 일곱 살에 대학 수업을 들은 신동을 만났어요.
examples.en: I met a prodigy who took college classes at the age of seven.
Prodigies often become ordinary as they grow up.
This movie is about a Go prodigy.

explain: '천재'는 나이와 상관없이 뛰어난 사람이고, '신동'은 어린아이일 때 이미 어른 같은 재능을 보이는 아이예요. 보통 '피아노 신동', '수학 신동'처럼 분야 이름을 앞에 붙여요. 어른에게는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: That child is famous as a music prodigy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분야 이름을 앞에 붙여 쓰는 가장 흔한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, with the field name in front.

phrases.example: 여섯 살 수학 신동이 텔레비전에 나왔어요.
phrases.en: A six-year-old math prodigy appeared on TV.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린데도 어른처럼 계산을 잘하는 아이에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a young child who calculates like an adult.

phrases.en: The boy genius won first place in the contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신동'과 비슷하지만 '천재'는 나이와 상관없이 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 신동, but 천재 can be used at any age.

explain_en: '천재' is an outstanding person at any age, while '신동' is a child who already shows adult-level talent. A field is usually put in front: '피아노 신동', '수학 신동'. It is not used for adults.

examples.ko: 이 가수는 노래를 정말 잘하는 실력파예요.
examples.en: This singer is a truly skilled performer who sings really well.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에는 실력파 신입 사원이 들어왔어요.
examples.en: A talented new employee joined our team.

examples.ko: 그 식당 주방장은 요리 실력파로 유명해요.
examples.en: The chef at that restaurant is famous as a real master of cooking.

examples.ko: 요즘은 실력파 밴드가 인기를 얻고 있어요.
examples.en: These days skilled bands are getting popular.

examples.ko: 실력파가 모인 대회라서 경기가 정말 재미있었어요.
examples.en: The match was really fun because it was a tournament full of skilled players.

examples.ko: 저는 얼굴보다 실력파 배우의 연기를 보러 가요.
examples.en: I go to see the acting of skilled actors rather than good looks.

explain: '실력파'는 겉모습이나 인기보다 실제 솜씨로 인정받는 사람에게 써요. 보통 가수, 배우, 선수, 요리사처럼 기술이 중요한 직업 앞에 붙여서 '실력파 가수', '실력파 신인'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 연기를 정말 잘하는 실력파 배우예요.
phrases.en: That person is a really skilled actor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인기보다 연기 실력으로 인정받는 배우를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An actor recognized for acting skill rather than popularity.

phrases.en: This restaurant has a highly skilled chef.
phrases.nuance_ko: 솜씨가 중요한 직업 앞에 붙여 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be put before jobs where skill matters.

phrases.en: That band is famous as a group of skilled players.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-로 유명하다'를 붙여 평판을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-로 유명하다' to talk about a reputation.

explain_en: Performer or worker known for skill, not looks. 실력파 is used for people recognized for real skill rather than looks or popularity. It usually goes in front of jobs where skill matters, such as singers, actors, athletes, and chefs, as in 실력파 가수 and 실력파 신인.

examples.en: That teacher cherished me as a favorite student.
He is a famous painter's favorite student.
It's an honor to be called the teacher's favorite student.
The professor sent his favorite student abroad to study.

examples.ko: 애제자가 큰 상을 받아서 스승님이 기뻐하셨어요.
examples.en: The master was delighted that his favorite student won a big prize.

examples.ko: 저는 선생님 애제자는 아니었지만 많이 배웠어요.
examples.en: I wasn't the teacher's favorite student, but I learned a lot.

explain: 스승이 특별히 아끼는 제자를 말해요. 스승이 제자를 소개할 때 자연스럽고, 자기 입으로 '저는 애제자예요'라고 하면 자랑처럼 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The teacher took him as a favorite student.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스승이 특별히 아끼며 제자로 받아들인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a teacher takes someone in as a specially cherished student.
phrases.en_equiv: to take as a favorite student

phrases.en: The professor's favorite student won an award.
phrases.nuance_ko: '애제자'보다 쉬운 말로 풀어서 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plainer way to say 'aejeja'.

phrases.en: He was that painter's favorite student.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 관계를 소개할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Natural when introducing someone else's relationship.

explain_en: It refers to a student a teacher particularly cherishes. It sounds natural when others or the teacher say it, but calling yourself '애제자' can sound like bragging.

examples.en: My father is a well-known devoted husband.

examples.ko: 그는 아내 말이라면 뭐든 들어주는 애처가예요.
examples.en: He is a doting husband who does whatever his wife says.

examples.ko: 애처가로 유명한 배우가 아내에게 꽃을 선물했어요.
examples.en: The actor, famous as a devoted husband, gave his wife flowers.
My husband is devoted to me, so he helps with all the housework.

examples.ko: 남자 친구가 나중에 애처가가 될 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think my boyfriend will be a devoted husband later on.
Thanks to my devoted husband, I'm always happy.

explain: 아내를 아끼고 사랑하는 남편을 말해요. 아내를 무서워하는 남편을 뜻하는 '공처가'와 헷갈리지 마세요. 일상에서는 '아내 바보'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 그는 아내를 잘 챙겨서 애처가 소리를 들어요.
phrases.en: He takes such good care of his wife that people call him a doting husband.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주변에서 애처가라고 말할 만큼 아내를 아낀다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means he cares for his wife so much that others call him a doting husband.
phrases.en_equiv: to be called a doting husband

phrases.en: He is known at work as a doting husband.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주변 사람들이 다 알 만큼 아내를 아낀다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when everyone around knows he cares deeply for his wife.
phrases.en_equiv: to be known as a doting husband

phrases.en: My uncle is totally smitten with his wife.
phrases.nuance_ko: '애처가'보다 편한 구어이고, 친한 사이에서 웃으며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual, colloquial term used with a smile among close people.

explain_en: Husband who loves and cherishes his wife; positive, admiring. It refers to a husband who cherishes and loves his wife. Don't confuse it with '공처가', a husband who is afraid of his wife. In daily talk people also say '아내 바보'.

examples.ko: 저는 오래된 영화를 좋아하는 영화 애호가예요.
examples.en: I'm a film buff who loves old movies.

examples.ko: 커피 애호가들이 이 가게를 많이 찾아요.
examples.en: Many coffee enthusiasts visit this shop.
A concert for classical music lovers is being held.
He is known as a tea enthusiast.

examples.ko: 책 애호가라면 이 서점을 좋아할 거예요.
examples.en: If you love books, you will like this bookstore.
I went to a photography enthusiasts' meeting for the first time.

explain: '애호가'는 어떤 취미나 분야를 오래 깊이 좋아하는 사람이에요. '팬'은 특정 사람이나 팀을 좋아할 때, 애호가는 영화, 커피, 음악 같은 분야를 좋아할 때 자주 써요. '전문가'는 일로 잘 아는 사람이라 달라요.

phrases.en: I am a classical music enthusiast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분야 이름 뒤에 붙여 그 분야를 깊이 좋아하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach it after a field to mean someone who deeply loves it.

phrases.en: I went to a meeting where tea lovers gather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 취미를 가진 사람들을 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a group of people who share a hobby.

phrases.en: This hobby has many enthusiasts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 취미나 분야의 인기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about how popular a hobby or field is.

explain_en: An 애호가 is someone who deeply loves a hobby or field over a long time. 팬 is usually for a specific person or team, while 애호가 fits fields like film, coffee or music. A 전문가 is someone who knows a field professionally, which is different.

t90.ax: He is known as a tea enthusiast.

en: to be respectable; to be proper

examples.en: I've become a proper university student now.
My younger sibling has settled in as a full-fledged working adult.
It was a small shop, but they put up a proper sign.
The child has become a proper young lady before I knew it.

examples.ko: 어엿한 회사원이 되고 나니 부모님이 기뻐하세요.
examples.en: Now that I'm a proper office worker, my parents are happy.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 이제 어엿한 맛집이 됐어요.
examples.en: That restaurant has become a proper famous eatery.

explain: 남 앞에 내놓아도 부끄럽지 않게 번듯하고 당당하다는 느낌이에요. 보통 '어엿한 대학생', '어엿한 어른'처럼 신분이나 자격을 나타내는 명사 앞에서 써요. 어리거나 작던 것이 자라서 인정받을 만해졌을 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: You've become a proper adult now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자라서 어른답게 인정받을 만해졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone has grown up enough to be seen as a real adult.

phrases.en: The child has grown up well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부끄럽지 않게 번듯하게 큰 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes growing up in a respectable way.

phrases.en: You look quite respectable in a suit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모습이 번듯하고 당당해 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks decent and confident.

explain_en: It gives the feeling of being presentable and confident enough to show to others without embarrassment. It usually appears before a noun of status or qualification, like '어엿한 대학생' or '어엿한 어른'. It fits when something young or small has grown into something worthy of recognition.

examples.en: The stage director gave instructions to the actors.

examples.ko: 그 연출가는 새로운 뮤지컬을 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: That director is preparing a new musical.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 연출가가 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I've wanted to become a director since I was young.
The director's intention was well shown on stage.
After the show, the director came out to greet the audience.
The director and the writer revised the script together.

explain: 연극, 뮤지컬, 방송에서 전체 장면과 배우의 움직임을 이끄는 사람이에요. 영화는 보통 '감독'이라고 하고, 방송은 'PD'나 '연출'이라고 해요. '연출가'는 무대 쪽에서 가장 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I met a famous stage director.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연출가는 무대 쪽에서 가장 자연스러워서 '연극'과 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 연출가 is most natural for the stage, so it is often paired with 연극.

phrases.en: He is in charge of directing this musical.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연이나 방송에서 연출 일을 책임질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone takes charge of directing a show or program.
phrases.en_equiv: to be in charge of directing

phrases.example: 그 감독은 영화를 세 편 만들었어요.
phrases.en: That director has made three movies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화에서는 '연출가'보다 '감독'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For films, 감독 is used instead of 연출가.

explain_en: Director of plays or stage works; refers to the profession. 연출가 leads the whole production and the actors' movements in theater, musicals and broadcasts. For film Koreans usually say 감독, and for TV 'PD' or 연출. 연출가 sounds most natural for stage work.

t90.ax: That director is preparing a new musical.

examples.en: My friend is a well-known movie buff.
I'm a movie buff, so I go to the theater every weekend.
I went to a meetup where movie buffs gather.

examples.ko: 저는 영화광이 아니라서 유명한 배우도 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: I'm not a movie buff, so I don't know the famous actors well.

examples.ko: 영화광 삼촌이 추천해 준 영화를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the movie my movie-buff uncle recommended.

examples.ko: 영화광인 언니는 한 해에 백 편을 봐요.
examples.en: My older sister, a movie buff, watches a hundred films a year.

explain: 영화를 아주 좋아해서 많이 보는 사람이에요. '야구광', '축구광'처럼 '-광'이 붙으면 그것을 열렬히 좋아하는 사람이라는 뜻이 돼요.

phrases.example: 저는 영화 마니아라서 극장에 자주 가요.
phrases.en: I'm a movie maniac, so I go to the theater often.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영화광'과 비슷한 말로, 말할 때 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 영화광, and comfortable to use in speech.

phrases.example: 그 영화를 본 뒤로 영화광이 되었어요.
phrases.en: After watching that movie, I became a movie buff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 계기로 영화를 아주 좋아하게 되었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something made you start loving movies.

phrases.example: 영화광들은 새 영화가 나오면 먼저 보러 가요.
phrases.en: Movie buffs go see new movies first when they come out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-들'을 붙여 여러 명의 영화 팬을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -들 refers to several movie fans.

explain_en: It is a person who loves movies and watches a lot of them. With '-광', as in '야구광' and '축구광', a word means someone who is passionately fond of that thing.

en: crown prince; heir to the throne

examples.ko: 조선 시대의 왕세자는 어릴 때부터 공부를 많이 했어요.
examples.en: A crown prince in the Joseon era studied a great deal from a young age.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 왕세자 역할을 맡은 배우가 인기예요.
examples.en: The actor who plays the crown prince in the drama is popular.
The crown prince sneaked out of the palace.
The British crown prince's wedding was on the news.
I saw items the crown prince used at the museum.

examples.ko: 왕세자에게 공부를 가르치는 스승이 따로 있었대요.
examples.en: I heard the crown prince had a separate teacher for his studies.

explain: 한국 사극에서는 '세자'라고 줄여 부르는 경우가 많고, 높여 부르는 말은 '세자 저하'예요. 영국처럼 지금도 왕이 있는 나라의 뉴스에서도 들을 수 있지만 일상 대화에는 거의 안 나와요.

phrases.en: In the historical drama, the prince greets the king.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사극에서 더 자주 쓰는 줄임말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form more often used in historical dramas.

phrases.en: He became crown prince at a young age.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리를 얻을 때 '되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'become' when taking on the position.

phrases.en: The king and the crown prince left the palace together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 왕실 이야기에서 짝으로 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Appears as a pair in stories about royalty.

explain_en: Heir of a king in any country, modern news (그 나라의 왕세자가 다음 달에 결혼식을 올린대요.) In Korean historical dramas it is often shortened to '세자', and the respectful form of address is '세자 저하'. You can hear it in news about countries that still have a monarchy, such as Britain, but it almost never comes up in everyday conversation.

t90.ax: The crown prince sneaked out of the palace.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 외지인에게 조금 불친절하다고 해요.
examples.en: They say this village is a bit unfriendly to outsiders.
In the tourist season, many outsiders come to visit.
Judging from the way he talked, he seemed like an outsider.
I'm not from around here, so I don't know the roads well.
Outsiders bought land, so housing prices went up.

examples.ko: 이곳에서 오래 살았는데도 아직 외지인으로 보는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Even though I've lived here a long time, some people still see me as an outsider.

explain: 그 지역에서 나고 자란 '토박이'나 '현지인'과 반대로 말해요. 다른 지역에서 온 사람이라는 느낌이 강해서, 말투에 따라 거리를 두는 느낌이 날 수 있어요. 직접 말할 때는 '다른 지역에서 오신 분'이라고 하면 부드러워요.

phrases.example: 이 동네에는 외지 사람이 많이 와요.
phrases.en: Many outsiders come to this neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '외지인'보다 조금 더 입말 같은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Slightly more conversational than '외지인'.

phrases.en: A person from another area asked me for directions.
phrases.nuance_ko: '외지인'을 풀어 말해서 덜 차갑게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Spelled out, it sounds less cold than '외지인'.

phrases.en: Locals and outsiders prepare the festival together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '토박이'와 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs the word with its opposite, '토박이'.

explain_en: Newcomer from another area; stands out in a village or small town. It is the opposite of '토박이' (native) or '현지인' (local). It strongly means someone from another region, so depending on tone it can feel distant. When speaking directly to someone, '다른 지역에서 오신 분' sounds softer.

t90.ax: Outsiders bought land, so housing prices went up.

examples.en: In the old tale, the hero defeated the monster.
The hero in the game is a high-level character.

examples.ko: 그 마을에는 용감한 용사의 동상이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a statue of a brave warrior in that village.
The kids played holding sticks like heroic warriors.
Everyone welcomed the warriors who returned from the war.

examples.ko: 책 속 용사에게 마법의 검이 있었어요.
examples.en: The hero in the book had a magic sword.

explain: '용사'는 판타지 이야기, 게임, 옛이야기에서 용감하게 싸우는 사람을 가리켜요. 실제로 큰일을 한 사람은 '영웅'이라고 불러요. '참전 용사'는 실제 전쟁에 나간 사람이라 뉴스에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: War veterans came to the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 전쟁에 나간 사람을 높여 부르는 말로 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful term for people who fought in a real war, often in the news.

phrases.en: A brave warrior saved the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛이야기나 게임에서 자주 듣는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often heard in old tales and games.

phrases.en: He fought to the end like a warrior.
phrases.nuance_ko: 용감한 사람을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a comparison for someone brave.

explain_en: '용사' is the brave fighter in fantasy stories, games and old tales. A real person who did something great is called a '영웅'. '참전 용사' (war veteran) appears often in the news.

examples.ko: 원예사가 정원의 꽃을 정성껏 돌보고 있어요.
examples.en: The gardener is carefully tending the flowers in the garden.

examples.ko: 저는 원예사가 되려고 농업 학교에 다니고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm attending an agricultural school to become a horticulturist.
I asked the gardener how to grow potted plants.
Thanks to the gardener's care, the garden became beautiful.
I met a famous horticulturist and listened to the lecture.

examples.ko: 이 공원에는 원예사 열 명이 일해요.
examples.en: Ten gardeners work in this park.

explain: 꽃, 채소, 정원수를 가꾸는 일을 하는 사람이에요. 정원 관리에 초점을 맞추면 '정원사'라고도 하고, 농사 전반은 '농부'라고 해요. 식물에 대한 전문 지식이 있는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: The gardener is trimming the trees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말로, 정원을 관리하는 일에 더 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that focuses more on taking care of a garden.

phrases.example: 전문 원예사는 식물의 병도 잘 알아요.
phrases.en: A professional gardener also knows plant diseases well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전문'을 붙여 지식과 경험이 있는 사람임을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '전문' stresses the person's knowledge and experience.

phrases.en: My plant was wilting, so I asked a gardener.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물 관리가 고민일 때 도움을 구하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking an expert for help with plant care.

explain_en: Professional of plant cultivation, more technical/career term. This is a person who grows flowers, vegetables or garden trees as a job. When the focus is on looking after a garden, '정원사' is also used, and for farming in general it is '농부'. It carries a feel of specialized plant knowledge.

t90.ax: Ten gardeners work in this park.

examples.ko: 이 드라마의 원작자는 유명한 웹툰 작가예요.
examples.en: The original author of this drama is a famous webtoon artist.
The original author even wrote the film script personally.

examples.ko: 영화가 원작자의 뜻과 달라서 논란이 됐어요.
examples.en: The film caused controversy because it differed from the original author's intent.

examples.ko: 노래를 쓰려면 원작자에게 허락을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To use the song, you have to get permission from the original creator.
I want to meet the original author and hear their story.

examples.ko: 영상 설명에 원작자 이름이 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The original creator's name is written in the video description.

explain: 소설, 만화, 노래처럼 처음 만든 사람을 말할 때 써요. 영화나 드라마로 바뀐 작품에서 '원작'은 작품, '원작자'는 그 작품을 쓴 사람이에요. 그냥 글쓴이는 '작가', 그림을 그린 사람은 '화가'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I sang the song after getting the original creator's permission.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품을 쓸 때 필요한 허락을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the permission needed to use a work.

phrases.en: The original author and the director gave an interview together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 드라마 이야기에서 만든 사람들을 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the people behind a film or drama together.

phrases.example: 그분은 이 소설의 원작자로 알려져 있어요.
phrases.en: He is known as the original author of this novel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 처음 만들었는지 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to introduce who first created the work.

explain_en: It names the person who first created a novel, comic, or song. For a work adapted into a film or drama, '원작' is the work and '원작자' is the person who wrote it. A plain writer is '작가', and someone who paints is a '화가'.

examples.ko: 은퇴자 모임에서 매주 같이 등산을 가요.
examples.en: The retirees' group goes hiking together every week.
Many retirees live in this neighborhood.

examples.ko: 은퇴자를 위한 무료 컴퓨터 수업이 열려요.
examples.en: A free computer class for retirees is being offered.

examples.ko: 그분은 은퇴자 같지 않게 아주 젊어 보여요.
examples.en: He looks very young for a retiree.
The biggest worry for a retiree is living expenses.

examples.ko: 많은 은퇴자가 시골로 내려가 작은 밭을 가꿔요.
examples.en: Many retirees move to the countryside and tend a small field.

explain: 일을 그만두고 쉬는 사람을 말할 때 '은퇴자'를 쓰고, '퇴직자'도 비슷하게 써요. 운동선수나 연예인에게는 '은퇴하다'라는 동사를 자주 써요. 보통 '은퇴자 모임', '은퇴자 생활'처럼 다른 명사와 붙여 말해요.

phrases.en: I went to a retirees' gathering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '은퇴자'와 비슷하게 일을 그만둔 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 은퇴자, meaning someone who left their job.

phrases.en: Life after retirement is busier than I thought.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 그만둔 뒤의 생활을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for life after leaving work.

phrases.en: My father retired last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '은퇴자'와 짝이 되는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb that pairs with 은퇴자.

explain_en: '은퇴자' is used for someone who has stopped working, and '퇴직자' is used in a similar way. For athletes and entertainers, the verb '은퇴하다' is common. It often joins other nouns, as in '은퇴자 모임' or '은퇴자 생활'.
